summary: Describes a profile of IMAP and mail submission: a set of required extensions, restrictions and usage modes that lets clients with limited memory, bandwidth or processing power access and submit mail efficiently. It was a standards-track document and was replaced by RFC 5550.

eli5.summary: A phone with little power needs a lighter way to use email. This sets out a short list of email features that make it work smoothly for small devices.

questions: how do you forward email without downloading it
what imap extensions does lemonade require
subtitle: A profile of IMAP and SMTP for clients with limited resources to send and receive email.

tldr.problem: Mobile and embedded devices with limited memory, bandwidth, and processing power struggle to use standard IMAP and SMTP efficiently because they must download and upload entire messages.
tldr.mechanism: The Lemonade profile requires a specific set of IMAP and SMTP extensions (CATENATE, URLAUTH, BURL, CONDSTORE, NAMESPACE) and usage patterns that allow clients to forward messages without downloading them, reduce round-trips, and resynchronize efficiently.
tldr.outcome: Mobile clients can now handle email operations with less bandwidth and processing burden, but RFC 5550 provides the updated version of this profile.

today: RFC 4550 was a Proposed Standard published in June 2006. It was obsoleted by RFC 5550, which provides an updated profile with additional guidance for mobile email clients.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
The Lemonade profile addresses the needs of Internet email clients that operate in constrained environments. The name "Lemonade" stands for "Internet Email to Support Diverse Service Environments." The profile defines required extensions, restrictions, and usage modes for both IMAP and mail submission (SMTP) protocols.

Three main capabilities distinguish Lemonade: "forward without download" allows sending a received message to another address without downloading it to the client; quick resynchronization helps clients recover efficiently after losing connectivity; and bandwidth-saving IMAP and SMTP extensions reduce round-trips and data transfers.
sections.eli5: Lemonade is a special way to use email designed for phones and weak computers. It has three tricks: send email you haven't downloaded, catch up fast after losing connection, and use fewer messages back and forth.

sections.title: Forward Without Download
sections.content:
The most distinctive feature of Lemonade is "forward without download." Traditionally, forwarding a message requires the client to download the entire message, then upload it with the submission server. In Lemonade, the client sends a reference (a URLAUTH URL) pointing to the message on the IMAP server instead.

Two approaches are supported. The first uses the IMAP CATENATE extension to compose and assemble messages on the IMAP server itself, storing a draft and then sending a URL to the submission server. The second uses SMTP CHUNKING and BURL commands to submit new content alongside references to existing content. Both approaches require the IMAP server to advertise URLAUTH, CATENATE, and UIDPLUS, and the submission server to support BURL with URLAUTH-format URLs.
sections.eli5: Instead of copying the whole email, the client just gives the server a special link to the email. The server follows the link to get a copy without the client having to download it first.

sections.title: Message Submission and Synchronization
sections.content:
Lemonade submission servers must support several SMTP extensions to operate efficiently: PIPELINING to avoid round-trips, DSN for delivery status notifications, SIZE for message size declaration, ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES for detailed error reporting, and STARTTLS for encryption. The client can declare the size of a message upfront, allowing the server to reject it before transmission begins if it exceeds limits.

For synchronization, Lemonade IMAP servers must support the CONDSTORE extension, which tracks modification sequences and allows clients to quickly learn what flag changes have occurred since the last synchronization point. This enables efficient reconnection after temporary network loss.
sections.eli5: The email system lets the phone do several things at once to save time, tells it if the email arrived safely, and remembers which emails changed so the phone doesn't have to download everything again.

sections.title: Required IMAP Extensions
sections.content:
Beyond CONDSTORE, CATENATE, UIDPLUS, and URLAUTH, Lemonade IMAP servers must support NAMESPACE for discovering shared mailboxes and user mailboxes, LITERAL+ to save a round-trip when sending long strings, and IDLE for receiving instant notifications about mailbox changes. All Lemonade servers must support IMAP over TLS.

A special IMAP keyword, $Forwarded, was registered to mark messages that have been resent to another address. Clients set this flag when a forward succeeds, typically to display a different icon. The servers must preserve this flag during COPY operations and support searching for it.
sections.eli5: The phone can see shared mailboxes, send long messages in one step, get instant alerts when new mail arrives, and mark a message as forwarded.

sections.title: Security and Overview
sections.content:
The URLAUTH mechanism includes a "pawn-ticket" authorization system: the client creates a time-limited URL containing its own authorization credentials, allowing the submission server to fetch message content without needing direct access to the user's mailbox. The client can revoke access or set expiration times. Both the client-to-IMAP and submission-to-IMAP connections should use TLS to protect the URLAUTH token from interception and replay attacks.

Authentication for IMAP and submission follows the mandatory mechanisms defined in RFC 3501 and RFC 4409. The fcc (file carbon copy) problem of saving sent messages is addressed through CATENATE, which can compose the final message on the server in a single operation.
sections.eli5: The phone gives the email server a temporary permission slip to fetch one email, which the server can use but then cannot reuse. Using encryption keeps the permission slip secret.

items.title: Forward without download
items.text: Send received messages by reference instead of downloading and uploading.

items.title: Quick resynchronization
items.text: Learn only what changed since last check using CONDSTORE.

items.title: Bandwidth saving
items.text: Use extensions like PIPELINING, LITERAL+, and IDLE to reduce round-trips.
